title: Tech Note: NULLS in 4D v11 SQL
author: Chris Visaya, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Field properties (Reject NULL, Map NULL to blank)
SQL NULL handling (IS NULL, IS NOT NULL)

historical_commentary.text: This technical note provides a foundational explanation of NULL value handling in 4D v11 SQL, a critical SQL compatibility feature that distinguished 4D v11 from earlier versions. The note clearly articulates when NULLs are useful (aggregate functions like AVG/SUM/MIN/MAX must correctly exclude unknown values to avoid mathematical errors), explains the field-level properties for controlling NULL behavior (Reject NULL, Map NULL to blank), and documents the 4D language commands (IS FIELD VALUE NULL, SET FIELD VALUE NULL) and SQL commands (IS NULL, IS NOT NULL) for working with NULLs. While the core concepts of NULL values remain valid and essential to SQL, modern ORDA (4D v2018+) abstracts much of this low-level SQL detail away from everyday developers, who typically interact with typed entity attributes rather than raw NULL fields. However, understanding NULLs remains crucial for database design and SQL queries.
related_updates: ORDA (4D v2018+) provides typed entity classes that abstract NULL handling, allowing developers to work with more explicit Optional types and validation rules rather than raw NULLs
Modern 4D's SQL layer (accessed via ORDA queries and REST APIs) retains NULL semantics, but most everyday developers interact through ORDA rather than direct SQL
Data validation frameworks (constraints, attribute rules, calculated properties) in modern ORDA provide richer alternatives to raw NULL handling for most use cases
The core SQL NULL semantics described here (IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, aggregate function behavior) remain completely valid and unchanged in modern 4D SQL
